rules: Exact prose-literal substitutions only in revision 18 presentation; historical revisions remain unchanged. Preserve mechanics, NPC knowledge values and ledger actions.

entries.old: Daniel Kessler is waiting beside your desk, making no effort to pretend the meeting is accidental. Thirty-two, long-limbed and permanently one button short of Axiom’s dress code, he has dark curls that resist corporate grooming and a face that usually gives away the joke before he tells it. There is no joke this morning.
entries.new: Daniel Kessler waits beside your desk. His collar is open, his dark curls untidy; usually the joke reaches his face before he says a word. This morning he watches you approach without smiling.
entries.reason: Stronger voice and specificity; unchanged event and branch meaning.

entries.old: Daniel has worked two desks over from me for four years. Clever, indiscreet, kinder than he wants anyone to notice. I am grateful he told me himself—and angry that I am hearing it from him instead of Benton.
entries.new: Four years, two desks away. Daniel can never quite keep a secret. This one should have come from Benton.
entries.reason: Stronger voice and specificity; unchanged event and branch meaning.

entries.old: Benton is fifty-eight, compact and silver-haired, his charcoal suit so precisely fitted that it seems less like clothing than policy. He never hurries. He has built a career out of making everyone else adjust their pace to his.
entries.new: Compact and silver-haired, Benton wears a charcoal suit without a crease out of place. He never hurries. He has built a career out of making everyone else adjust their pace to his.
entries.reason: Stronger voice and specificity; unchanged event and branch meaning.

entries.old: Benton has supervised me for four years. He praises precision when it protects him and calls it overthinking when it does not. He has not mentioned the promotion, and his arrival makes disappointment harden into suspicion. He almost never brings an assignment to someone’s desk himself.
entries.new: Four years of Benton praising my precision when it protects him and calling it overthinking when it does not. He has come all the way to my desk with another assignment. Still nothing about the promotion.
entries.reason: Stronger voice and specificity; unchanged event and branch meaning.

entries.old: Maya Reyes crosses from the compliance wing carrying two paper cups. Thirty-three, with warm brown skin and watchful dark eyes, she wears her black hair in a loose knot and has turned back the cuffs of her navy suit. The small rebellion suits her. She sets one cup beside your terminal and keeps the other. No greeting. This is an old ritual.
entries.new: Maya Reyes crosses from compliance with two paper cups, the cuffs of her navy suit turned back. Loose strands of black hair escape her knot. Her dark eyes find yours as she sets one cup beside the terminal and keeps the other. No greeting. You know this ritual.
entries.reason: Stronger voice and specificity; unchanged event and branch meaning.

entries.old: I know the exact moment friendship became something else. I have spent two years pretending I do not. Even now, hurt and angry, part of me is simply relieved that she came.
entries.new: Two years of measuring what I say to her. Of knowing when to turn a look into a joke. This morning I have no joke ready. I am just glad she came.
entries.reason: Stronger voice and specificity; unchanged event and branch meaning.

entries.old: Maya is the colleague I trust more than anyone in this building. Trust is not intimacy, even when she keeps testing the boundary. Her arrival makes me feel less alone—and that is already more dependence than I intended.
entries.new: Maya is the colleague I trust most in this building. I can give her the version I would never put in a report. How much beyond that is mine to decide.
entries.reason: Removes unchosen dependency judgment and implied romantic intent from professional branch.

entries.old: Daniel nods. “Sure,” he says, in a tone that means he believes none of it.
entries.new: Daniel nods. “Sure.” He keeps his voice low. Neither of you moves on.
entries.reason: Stronger voice and specificity; unchanged event and branch meaning.

entries.old: I do not regret forcing him to say it aloud. I regret giving him one more chance to be honest with me.
entries.new: Next quarter. Another three months of doing the work while he decides whether I deserve the title.
entries.reason: Stronger voice and specificity; unchanged event and branch meaning.

entries.old: Maya’s expression softens. “I know. It should’ve been yours.”
entries.new: Maya’s expression softens. “I know.” For once she leaves the silence alone. “It should’ve been yours.”
entries.reason: Stronger voice and specificity; unchanged event and branch meaning.

entries.old: Inside, the tower remains visible beyond the rain. The apartment has the same narrow rooms, the same chair by the window, the same jacket that once meant a day at the office. The phone is warm in your hand. Upstairs, Marcus and Celeste spoke to this face as though it came with a history you could recall.
